items.title: Govt studying specific law to tackle ticket scalping
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Ministry, together with the Communications Ministry and relevant agencies, is reviewing specific legislation to address ticket scalping activities. She said such activities not only force consumers to pay exorbitant prices but may also expose them to the risk of fraud when purchasing tickets from unofficial sellers. Purchasing tickets from unofficial sellers could result in consumers receiving counterfeit tickets, tickets that have already been used, or tickets that have been cancelled by the organiser, she added.

items.title: Aireen Omar named AI Malaysia chairperson
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Aireen Omar, former AirAsia Bhd chief executive officer, has been appointed chairperson of AI Malaysia Bhd, the government's newly established agency tasked with spearheading and coordinating Malaysia's national artificial intelligence (AI) agenda. As the ministry's lead agency for AI, AI Malaysia is tasked with coordinating the national AI agenda, promoting safe and responsible AI adoption and driving the National AI Action Plan 2026–2030 towards achieving AI Nation 2030. Gobind said the appointment of AI Malaysia's inaugural board marked an important milestone in strengthening the institutional foundation for Malaysia's national AI agenda.

items.title: Porsche driver escapes unhurt after sports car consumed by flames at Lanchang toll plaza
items.summary: TEMERLOH: A Porsche sports car, believed to be a Cayman, was completely destroyed by fire at the Lanchang toll plaza exit ramp here today. Pahang Fire and Rescue Department assistant director of operations, Mohd Salahuddin Isa, said firemen were alerted to the incident at 1.04pm. He said that a team of eight firefighters from the Mentakab Fire and Rescue Station, along with a Fire Rescue Tender vehicle and an Emergency Medical Rescue Services unit, was dispatched to the scene.

items.title: DNA results for five Long Lellang crash victims due by tomorrow, say Sarawak police
items.summary: MIRI, Sept 11 — The deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) analysis for all five victims of the Flying Doctor Service helicopter crash in Long Lellang last Tuesday is expected to be completed by tomorrow at the latest. “We anticipate that the DNA analysis for the five victims could be completed by tomorrow at the latest,” he told reporters here today. Last Tuesday, a BO-105 helicopter carrying five people, including the pilot, crashed near the Long Lellang Short Take-Off and Landing Airport.

items.title: New York marks 25th anniversary of 9/11 attacks
items.summary: NEW YORK: New York commemorates the 25th anniversary of the devastating Sept 11, 2001 attacks Friday with a ceremony marked by US President Donald Trump's absence and right-wing outrage at the attendance of the city's first Muslim mayor. [[nid:1530584]] Trump will pay his respects at the Pentagon, not New York, where hijacked planes destroyed the World Trade Centre and killed most of the 2,977 total victims on that world-altering day. Alongside the former presidents will be Democratic Mayor Zohran Mamdani, the Big Apple's first Muslim mayor, despite a campaign urging him to stay away spearheaded by the right-wing New York Post and former mayor Rudy Giuliani.

items.title: MMEA conducts 720,000 inspections, detains 4,401 since 2023
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency (MMEA) has carried out about 720,000 inspections and 161 searches since 2023, detaining 4,401 people as part of efforts to combat cross-border crimes in the country's waters. MMEA Maritime Security and Surveillance Division Border Security and Data Branch principal assistant director Commander Mohd Khairul Azhar Isahak said illegal fishing, smuggling and the entry of illegal immigrants were among the main threats being tackled by the agency. Khairul said the effectiveness of MMEA operations depended greatly on cooperation from the maritime community, particularly fishermen, who played a key role as the agency's 'eyes and ears' in detecting suspicious movements and activities at sea.

items.title: Umno must end internal bickering, strengthen unity, says party delegate
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Umno should strengthen unity within the party and put an end to internal bickering and "backstabbing" as it rebuilds its political strength. Johor Umno delegate Mohd Fared Mohd Khalid said grievances should be raised through proper party channels instead of being discussed behind the backs of leaders and members. Fared, who is Parit Sulong Umno deputy chief, said members who were unhappy with any decision should voice their concerns in meetings or through delegates rather than create divisions within the party.

items.title: Newborn’s body found in Dungun hostel locker, police investigating
items.summary: DUNGUN, Sept 11 — A 19-year-old student allegedly hid her newborn baby’s body in a hostel locker after giving birth in a toilet at an educational institution here two days ago. Dungun district police chief Supt Nik Ab Halim Nik Mat said police received a report on the discovery of the body at 10.48pm yesterday. Investigations found that the student allegedly wrapped the baby in cloth, placed the body in a bag, and kept it in a hostel locker.

items.title: Numbak fire victims receive RM1,500 special federal aid
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today presented RM1,500 in special federal aid to each of the 111 heads of households affected by the Numbak fire. The blaze razed a stilt settlement covering Kampung Lok Buta, Kampung Lok Poring and Kampung Sabang Lama, spanning an estimated 260 metres by 380 metres. Anwar visited the centre before departing for Kota Kinabalu International Airport.

items.title: Pas welcomes 'blue-green' cooperation
items.summary: Pas deputy president Datuk Seri Tuan Ibrahim Tuan Man said the party believed any differences could be resolved if all parties were sincere and adhered to principles outlined by Allah. The Perikatan Nasional deputy chairman said Pas would discuss the matter at its party meeting before it was brought to the party's Syura Council for consideration. Tuan Ibrahim said Pas had long championed the agenda of penyatuan ummah (Muslim unity) for the future of Muslims and Malays in Malaysia.

items.title: Melaka assembly dissolution 'not far off', says Rauf
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Melaka state assembly could be dissolved soon, with Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh saying the time was "not far off". Speaking to reporters on the sidelines of the 2026 Umno general assembly here today, Rauf said preparations for the state election had been under way for the past two years. Asked if the state assembly would be dissolved this month, he said: "InsyaAllah (God willing)."

items.title: Asean, South Korea join forces on AI, digital health for resilient regional care
items.summary: Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad described South Korea as an invaluable partner in advancing Asean's digital health agenda, calling the collaboration a crucial step towards a shared vision of an Asean that works together for equitable, future-ready health systems. Meanwhile, ROK Vice Minister of Health and Welfare Lee Hyung Hoon, who co-chaired the meeting, said stronger digital health cooperation was crucial to bridging healthcare and digital gaps among Asean member states. He said digital health had become a central pillar of Asean–ROK health cooperation since both sides agreed to establish a health dialogue channel at the 2019 Asean–ROK Commemorative Summit.

items.title: Tanker driver, still hospitalised, charged with murder over Pahang crash that wiped out young family on Merdeka Day
items.summary: TEMERLOH, Sept 11 — A cement tanker driver receiving treatment at Hospital Sultan Haji Ahmad Shah was charged today with four counts of murder over a crash that killed four people on Aug 31. Zulkarnain is accused of having caused the deaths of Muhammad Nazatullah Nazmi, Nur Atiqah Sofiya Mohd Kazwan, Muhammad Armaan Nazeef Muhammad Nazatullah and Seow Beng Wai. He said Seow’s son, Sebastian Seow Jhen, 18, who was driving the Honda CR-V, and the tanker driver sustained serious injuries and were treated at Hospital Sultan Haji Ahmad Shah in Temerloh.

items.title: PM: MA63 must be made a national narrative
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim wants discussions on the Malaysia Agreement 1963 (MA63) to be turned into a national narrative. Anwar said that by transforming it into a national agenda, matters regarding the interests of Sabah and Sarawak would no longer be viewed merely as special considerations for the two states. This is vital because otherwise, it remains sectoral, requiring special discussions for Sabah and Sarawak every year.

items.title: Selangor sets Oct 26 as replacement holiday for Sultan’s Silver Jubilee
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Sept 11 — Selangor has declared October 25 a special public holiday to commemorate the silver jubilee of Sultan Sharafuddin Idris Shah’s reign. State Secretary Datuk Dr Ahmad Fadzli Ahmad Tajuddin said the holiday would be replaced on October 26 as the anniversary falls on a Sunday, The Star reported. He added that the holiday would be observed in the same way as the September 1 public holiday marking Selangor’s overall victory at Sukma 2026.

items.title: Private tutor charged with exposing 4-year-old to physical injury
items.summary: AYER KEROH: A 25-year-old private tutor today pleaded not guilty in the Sessions Court here to a charge of exposing a 4-year-old girl under her care to physical injury last year. Nur Dalila Salleh entered the plea after the charge was read before Judge Rohatul Akmar Abdullah. The accused posted bail.

items.title: Was bad weather to blame? Investigators dig into what brought down deadly Long Lellang chopper
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Sept 11 — The Air Accident Investigation Bureau has begun its investigation into the cause of the Flying Doctor Service helicopter crash in Long Lellang which claimed five lives, said Deputy Transport Minister Datuk Hasbi Habibollah. Hasbi said the ministry’s air accident investigation team was already at the crash site and was working to determine the cause of the tragedy. “We will wait for the report from the Air Accident Investigation Team.

items.title: PM Anwar visits Kampung Numbak fire victims, pledges aid
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Sept 11 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim visited and offered support to victims of the Kampung Numbak fire at the temporary relief centre at the Damai Multipurpose Hall here today. Anwar, accompanied by Sabah Chief Minister Datuk Seri Hajiji Noor, arrived at the relief centre at 1.30 pm and spent about 20 minutes meeting the victims. The Prime Minister was then briefed on the fire by Kota Kinabalu Mayor Datuk Seri Dr Sabin Samitah before handing over aid to the victims.

items.title: Zahid's speech was that of a prime minister-in-waiting, says KJ
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Khairy Jamaluddin said Umno president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi's policy speech showed that the party and Barisan Nasional were ready to form the next government. The former Umno Youth chief went as far as describing Zahid's policy speech as "the speech of a prime minister-in-waiting". "This is the speech of a prime minister-in-waiting, and a speech of a government-in-waiting," he said after Zahid delivered his presidential policy speech at the 2026 Umno General Assembly today.

items.title: Govt seeks more ideas to power auto sector
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The government is seeking greater industry input on policies, incentives and fiscal measures for the 2027 Budget to strengthen Malaysia's automotive sector. Finance Minister II Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan said the focus is on high-tech manufacturing, electric vehicles (EVs) and next-generation vehicles (NxGVs). He said strengthening the high-tech automotive sector could create more high-value jobs, enhance the country's export competitiveness and accelerate technology transfer and local talent development.

items.title: Zahid takes veiled swipe at Anwar over Budi95 quota flip-flop
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Umno president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi today took a veiled dig at Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim over the government's flip-flopping Budi Madani RON95 (Budi95) subsidised petrol quota. Zahid said the government had reduced the monthly quota for the fuel earlier this year, only to restore it last month. Guru," he said in his policy speech at the 2026 Umno General Assembly here today.

items.title: Mondelez invests RM90mil to expand capacity at Cadbury plant in Shah Alam
items.summary: SHAH ALAM: Mondelez International's RM90 million investment in its Cadbury plant in Selangor will expand production capacity to meet growing demand in both Malaysia andexport markets, according to Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari. The company's single largest investment at the Shah Alam confectionery plant was launched today with the completion of its new Crumb Tower. Amirudin said the investment also reflects Mondelez's confidence in Selangor as a long-term manufacturing base.

items.title: AI firm Anthropic detects fake accounts targeting Malaysian voters for manipulation
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: Malaysia has been targeted in an artificial intelligence (AI)-driven commercial manipulation operation involving more than 1,000 fake X accounts, voter data and constituency-based targeting systems aimed at influencing political sentiment. Anthropic, the company behind the Claude AI platform, exposed the operation in a report after finding an account had used its platform for election manipulation targeting Malaysian users. The report said the platform was built using Claude and marketed as a real-time, AI-powered political operations ecosystem.

items.title: Malaysia Day celebration to showcase unity, harmony across regions
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysia Day 2026 celebration, scheduled to be held at the Borneo Convention Centre Kuching (BCCK), Sarawak on Sept 16, will reflect the harmony and togetherness of Malaysians across the regions through the diversity of cultures and shared beliefs. Communications Ministry secretary-general Datuk Abdul Halim Hamzah said the uniqueness of this year's celebration would highlight the spirit of Segulai Sejalai (togetherness) through the unity of various races in a national-level official event. He said this manifestation of harmony would be showcased through the Majlis Kesyukuran involving various faiths organised by the Unit for Other Religions (UNIFOR) on Sept 14, which would demonstrate unity among followers of various religions.

items.title: Straits Energy to tighten grip on US-listed TMD Energy with 96pct voting control
items.summary: In a Bursa Malaysia filing today, Straits Energy said TMD Energy proposed to split its existing ordinary shares into Class A and Class B shares. Under the exercise, 10 million TMD Energy shares held by Straits Energy will be converted into Class B shares on a one-for-one basis, while all other issued shares will become Class A shares. Straits Energy will also hold another 5.34 million Class A shares.

items.title: UMS professor acquitted of 21 false claims charges
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU: A university professor walked free from the Special Corruption Court today after being acquitted on 21 charges of making false claims for research funds related to Sabah's marine life. Sessions Court Judge Jason Juga discharged and acquitted Prof Dr Charles Santhanaraju Vairappan after finding that the prosecution had failed to prove a prima facie case against him on all the charges under Section 18 of the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission Act 2009. Charles claimed trial to all 21 charges on July 20, 2022.

items.title: Zahid: Umno proposing ‘Grand Collaboration’ to end political clashes in Malaysia
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 11 — A proposal for the formation of a “Grand Collaboration” through political understanding (Tafahum Siyasi) among the country’s political party coalitions has been put forward to avoid political clashes that would be detrimental to the ummah and the nation, said Umno president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi. He said the concept does not involve a merger of political parties, but rather a common ground for mutual understanding aimed at preserving political stability and reinvigorating national economic growth. In other words, whoever Umno and Barisan Nasional (BN) work with, Umno remains Umno, and Barisan Nasional remains Barisan Nasional,” he said.

items.title: Driver charged with murder over 11-vehicle crash that killed four
items.summary: TEMERLOH: A lorry driver was charged with murdering four people in an 11-vehicle crash along the East Coast Expressway on the night of Aug 31. The charge against Zulkarnain Md Noh, 52, was read out before Magistrate Nuur Fakhizaa Abu Bakar during a court proceeding held at Hospital Sultan Haji Ahmad Shah. Zulkarnain was charged with the murders of Muhammad Nazatullah Nazmi, 32, his wife Nur Atiqah Sofiya Mohd Kazwan, their son, Muhammad Armaan Nazeef, 4, and Seow Beng Wai, 55.

items.title: Baja 3 probe: Mat Sabu says yet to be called in by MACC
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Agriculture and Food Security Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Sabu has not been called in by the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) to assist in investigations into alleged delays in the supply of Additional Padi Compound Fertiliser 3 (Baja 3) to farmers in Kedah. Mohamad said he and the Agriculture and Food Security Ministry were ready to give their cooperation to the authorities if required. If required, the ministry and I are ready to give our full cooperation to the authorities," he said when contacted today.

items.title: Anwar to announce interim payment for Sarawak on Malaysia Day
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim is set to announce an interim payment to Sarawak related to the Malaysia Agreement 1963 on Malaysia Day, Sept 16. Anwar said discussions on the matter with Sarawak Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Tun Openg would continue over the next few days. Abang Johari, Sabah Chief Minister Datuk Seri Hajiji Noor and Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Sabah and Sarawak) Datuk Mustapha Sakmud were involved in the meeting.

items.title: GTA Holdings seals Brunei expansion with Safran Helicopter Engines distributorship
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: GTA Holdings Bhd has formalised its expansion into Brunei after securing a distributorship for selected Safran Helicopter Engines products and services in the neighbouring country. This follows plans first announced in July, when GTA's subsidiary signed a memorandum of understanding with Safran Helicopter Engines Asia to expand their partnership beyond Malaysia into Brunei. The company today said its wholly-owned unit, Global Turbine Asia Sdn Bhd, had signed a distributor agreement with Safran Helicopter Engines Asia.

items.title: Indonesia sees continued volcanic activity, multiple eruptions recorded
items.summary: JAKARTA: Multiple volcanic eruptions were recorded across Indonesia on Friday, with Mount Ili Lewotolok erupting six times and sending ash as high as 700m above its summit, while Mount Semeru and Mount Ibu also remained active. The Volcanology and Geological Hazard Mitigation Centre (PVMBG) said Ili Lewotolok in East Nusa Tenggara, which remains at Level II in Indonesia's four-tier volcano alert system, recorded the eruptions between 12.57am and 9.06am local time. Mount Semeru in East Java, which remains at Level III, the second-highest alert level, erupted four times between 12.26am and 6.16am, while Mount Ibu in North Maluku, which remains at Level II, recorded three eruptions between 12.49am and 8.58am, according to the data.

items.title: Man found dead in drain near SMK Tun Hussein Onn in Prai
items.summary: PRAI: The body of a 37-year-old man was found in a 1.5m-deep drain near SMK Tun Hussein Onn here today. Penang Fire and Rescue Department assistant operations director John Sagun Francis said firefighters received a request from police at 12.10pm to recover the body. "Five firefighters recovered the body and handed it over to police."

items.title: HE Group outlook brightens on data centre, semiconductor growth
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: HE Group Bhd's outlook remains positive underpinned by its strong data centre (DC) tender pipeline and growing semiconductor sector involvement, said Public Investment Bank Bhd (PublicInvest). "This lifts HE Group's outstanding orderbook to about RM317.3 million, while its tenderbook stands at about RM1 billion (80 per cent DC-related)." The firm said HE Group's RM317.3 million outstanding orderbook and robust RM1 billion tenderbook provide earnings visibility in the near to medium term.

items.title: Ku Li calls on ex-Umno members to return, strengthen party
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Umno veteran Tengku Razaleigh Hamzah has welcomed calls for former members to return to the party, saying Umno needs a "big family" to pool ideas to address challenges facing the Malay community. Tengku Razaleigh, better known as Ku Li, said those who had left the party should be welcomed back as Umno needed their contributions and experience. We welcome all of them to return to Umno.

items.title: RM2.4b drug lab: Police hunt 4 to 5 more suspects
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Police are hunting four to five more syndicate members linked to the RM2.4 billion drug laboratory busted recently, with some believed to have fled the country. Narcotics Crime Investigation Department (NCID) director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said investigators had identified the suspects and efforts were underway to track them down. The hunt follows investigations into the syndicate linked to the large-scale drug laboratory, where drugs worth an estimated RM2.4 billion were uncovered.

items.title: Woman injured as car hits raised road fixture, overturns in PJ
items.summary: "Initial investigations found that the vehicle's left tyre ran over a raised fixture, causing the underside of the vehicle to hit the metal before the driver lost control and the car overturned. The department said preliminary investigations found that the accident was caused by the poorly maintained road fixture, which resulted in the driver losing control of the vehicle. The vehicle was taken to the Petaling Jaya district police headquarters TEID.

items.title: Anwar agrees Sarawak deserves fair share, promises formula clarity, interim measure by Malaysia Day
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Sept 11 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim agreed to work towards establishing a formula for Sarawak to receive a share of the state’s revenue as he prepares to discuss an interim measure with Sarawak Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Openg. Anwar said Sarawak had put forward its views on a formula that would provide greater clarity on the matter, taking into account the federal government’s financial position and capacity. Anwar said he would continue discussions with Abang Johari over the next few days and hoped to announce an interim measure for Sarawak around the Malaysia Day celebrations in Kuching on September 16.

items.title: Sabah gets RM1.5b MA63 boost, Anwar hints Sarawak could be next by Sept 16
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Sept 11 — The interim allocation for Sabah will immediately rise to RM1.5 billion this year, said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. He said this in reply to a request from Sabah Chief Minister Datuk Seri Panglima Hajiji Noor during the Malaysia Agreement 1963 (MA63) Implementation Action Council meeting (MTPMA63) press conference here. That is on behalf of the Sabah government,” said Hajiji.

items.title: From complaint to compensation: How victims in Malaysia are winning sexual harassment cases
items.summary: SEMPORNA, Sept 11 — The Sexual Harassment Tribunal Agency (Tags) under the Ministry of Women, Family and Community Development (KPWKM) recorded 134 sexual harassment complaints over a two-year period, with 90 of them successfully resolved. Male victims and children can also use this platform to seek redress. “Some victims have also won their cases and received compensation,” she told reporters after officiating the Semporna Zero Tolerance for Violence: Advocacy Against Sexual Harassment and End Violence Against Women programmes here yesterday.

items.title: DNA tests pending for five victims of Long Lellang helicopter crash, says Sarawak police
items.summary: KUCHING, Sept 11 — The post-mortems on all five victims of the Flying Doctor Service helicopter crash in Long Lellang last Tuesday were completed at 7.30pm yesterday. Sarawak Police Commissioner Datuk Mohamad Zainal Abdullah said the cause of death for all five victims was severe burn injuries sustained in the helicopter crash. On Tuesday, the Civil Aviation Authority of Malaysia said a BO-105 helicopter carrying five individuals, including the pilot, had crashed near the Long Lellang Short Take-Off and Landing Airport.

items.title: Perak orders caterer at Lenggong boarding school to shut after almost 160 students, staff fall sick
items.summary: IPOH, September 11 — A food caterer serving a boarding school in Lenggong, Perak has been ordered to close after 159 students and staff developed symptoms of suspected food poisoning. Perak Health, Human Resources, Indian Affairs and National Integration Committee chairman Datuk A. Sivanesan said the Hulu Perak District Health Office received a report of the incident from Lenggong Health Clinic on September 10. Sivanesan also urged food handlers to comply with the Food Act 1983 and Food Hygiene Regulations 2009 to prevent further food poisoning incidents.

items.title: No U-turn: Ex-minister Dr Zaliha says she has backed Health Service Commission proposal since 2023
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 11 — Former Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Zaliha Mustafa today denied making a U-turn on the proposal to establish a Health Service Commission, saying she had remained committed to the initiative since 2023. In a statement, Dr Zaliha said that as early as February 2023, she had publicly stated that the proposal to establish the commission was among the key matters being considered in the final draft of the Health White Paper. “In fact, in April 2023, the same news portal reported on my meeting with representatives of Hartal Doktor Kontrak (HDK), where the proposal to establish a Health Service Commission and a Health Reform Commission was discussed within the framework of the White Paper,” she said.

items.title: Anwar: Time to make MA63 part of the national conversation, not just Sabah-Sarawak issue
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Sept 11 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim wants the implementation of the Malaysia Agreement 1963 (MA63) to become part of the national narrative rather than being viewed solely as an issue concerning Sabah and Sarawak. He said the approach was important to ensure Malaysians understood that the government’s commitment to MA63 formed part of the Madani Government’s national policy and was closely linked to the country’s development, stability and unity. Anwar said this must be understood and embraced by people in peninsular Malaysia, Sabah and Sarawak as part of a national policy, commitment and narrative aimed at strengthening the country.

items.title: Sounds like a ‘PM in waiting’, Khairy says of Zahid’s speech at Umno assembly
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 11 — Umno president Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi’s keynote at the party’s general assembly this morning earned praise from Khairy Jamaluddin. Khairy, an Umno returnee after being sacked three years ago for alleged disciplinary infractions and breaches of party discipline during GE15 – described the speech as crystal clear on Barisan Nasional’s (BN) direction ahead of the coming general election. “This is the speech of a prime minister in waiting and a speech of a government in waiting,” Khairy told reporters after Zahid’s speech at the 2026 Umno general assembly here.

items.title: Sabah, Sarawak to get bigger share of Parliament seats, Anwar says as MA63 push moves ahead
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Sept 11 — Sabah and Sarawak will get a higher proportion of parliamentary representation under a Cabinet decision in principle to increase the number of seats for the two Borneo states, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim announced today. Anwar said the Cabinet had agreed to increase the number of parliamentary seats for Sabah and Sarawak, although the exact number and mechanism had yet to be determined. Anwar added that there could also be an increase in seats for peninsular Malaysia.

items.title: Zahid says Umno still hopes for favourable outcome after Najib clemency deferred
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 11 — Umno president Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi today expressed disappointment over the postponement of former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak’s clemency application, but said the party continues to hope for a favourable outcome. Zahid said Umno respected the decision and would continue to uphold the institution of the Malay Rulers while appealing to His Majesty the King to use his wisdom in deciding Najib’s application. The Prime Minister’s Department today said Najib’s clemency application had been deferred to a future sitting of the Federal Territories Pardons Board.

items.title: State institutions won’t be political tools if BN returns to power, Zahid pledges at Umno assembly
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 11 — Umno president Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi today vowed that Malaysia’s courts and institutions would not be used as political tools if Barisan Nasional (BN) returns to Putrajaya. Zahid said the pledge was part of BN’s proposed “Agenda Malaysia Biru”, a roadmap of eight initiatives aimed at shaping the country as it approaches its centenary of independence. Zahid said the initiative aimed to place Malaysia among the world’s top 20 countries in terms of integrity, governance and the rule of law.

items.title: Zara Qairina inquest: Handwriting expert defends journal analysis despite rival’s differing testimony
items.summary: Nurul: No. Nurul: No. Nurul: Agree.

items.title: ‘Time has come for BN to lead’: Zahid demands GE16 held as soon as possible
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 11 — Umno president Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi today called for the 16th General Election (GE16) to be held as soon as possible, saying the time had come for Barisan Nasional (BN) to seek a fresh mandate to lead the country. Zahid said GE16 would be a defining moment for Umno and BN to regain the mandate to lead, as he outlined the coalition’s “gelombang biru” (blue wave) strategy ahead of the next general election. Since we are already fighting, let us fight all the way,” he said.

items.title: Health cooperation gets fresh push as Asean, China face new threats
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 11 — Asean and China are seeking to deepen their decade-long health cooperation as the region confronts emerging public health threats, climate change, demographic shifts and rapid technological transformation. Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad said the partnership is entering an increasingly consequential chapter, with both sides working towards resilient, inclusive and sustainable health systems capable of responding to present and future challenges. He said this in his opening remarks when chairing the 10th Asean-China Health Ministers’ Meeting in conjunction with the 17th Asean Health Ministers Meeting (AHMM) and Related Meetings here today.

items.title: Zahid takes swipe at Pakatan petrol promise, blasts Budi95 policy flip‑flop, says Umno primed for GE16
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 11 — Umno president Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi today took a veiled jibe at Pakatan Harapan’s past election manifesto to slash petrol prices within 24 hours if the coalition won the general election. Speaking at the 2026 Umno General Assembly today, Ahmad Zahid said Umno is a far-sighted party with a long-term vision for Malaysia rather than one that merely hopes to survive one election after another. Stressing that Umno would not make unrealistic promises, Zahid said: “We are also not a party that says, menang hari ini (win today)…” as the crowd responded, “minyak turun (fuel prices down)”.

items.title: Beyond data centres: What Budget 2027 needs to deliver, according to MBSB Investment Bank
items.summary: MBSB Investment Bank Bhd (MBSB IB) said there should also be focus on supply-side efficiency by broadening the tax base, closing leakages, expanding consumption excises, introducing carbon pricing, rationalising spending and crowding in private investment. “Budget 2027 should not only be assessed through fiscal expenditure. On the overall Budget 2027 allocation, MBSB IB said the budget is expected to remain moderately expansionary, with total federal government expenditure potentially reaching a new record of around RM440.9 billion, compared with Budget 2026’s RM421.2 billion.

items.title: No payslip, no problem? New housing policy targets gig workers
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 11 — Providing homeownership assistance, particularly for youths and gig workers, is among the key priorities of the National Housing Policy (DRN) 2026-2035, ensuring greater access to affordable housing. Ministry of Housing and Local Government (known by its Malay initials KPKT) Deputy Secretary-General (Housing and Urban Wellbeing) Zulkeflee Sulaiman said the Housing Credit Guarantee Scheme (SJKP) was among the mechanisms available to help first-time homebuyers without a fixed income or payslips. Meanwhile, KPKT Housing Planning Division undersecretary J. Murali said the ministry was refining the national affordable housing guidelines, with location being among the factors considered in determining prices.

items.title: Pardons Board postpones decision on Najib’s clemency application
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 11 — Former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak’s clemency application has been deferred to a future sitting of the Federal Territories Pardons Board, the Prime Minister’s Department’s Legal Affairs Division (BHEUU) said today. In a statement, it confirmed the board held its 63rd meeting this morning for Kuala Lumpur, Labuan and Putrajaya. “The Yang di-Pertuan Agong also consented for Datuk Seri Mohd Najib bin Tun Haji Abdul Razak’s application for pardon to be postponed to a Pardons Board meeting that will be held in the future,” BHEUU said.

items.title: Classic hits set upbeat tone as Umno assembly enters third day
items.summary: From classic hits such as Warisan by Datuk Sudirman, Ilham Pujangga by Ismail Haron as well as Seiring Sejalan by the late Datuk Sharifah Aini featuring the late Broery Marantika. The selection also reflects the renewed optimism within Umno’s ranks — elevated by Supreme Council member Datuk Seri Abdul Azeez Rahim joining the assembly after his release from remand. Aside from that, the assembly today also hosted four PAS leaders including its vice president Datuk Idris Ahmad, its secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan, PAS information chief Ahmad Fadhli Shaari and its assistant secretary-general Mohd Syahir Che Sulaiman.

items.title: A promise that cannot be kept: Grief and gratitude pour in for Sarawak's fallen medics
items.summary: MIRI, Sept 11 — “This story may soon be forgotten by others, bit by bit, but I will never forget you, not even for a second.” Those were the anguished words posted on Threads by izzatisyamimi, wife of pilot Captain Zainol Afiq Bee Sham, 30, who was among five people killed when a Flying Doctor Service (FDS) helicopter crashed near Long Lellang, Ulu Baram, on Sept 8. Captain Zainol Afiq Bee Sham, 30; medical officer Dr Ainul Baraah Kamaruddin, 33; assistant medical officer Alexson Adit Henry, 31; and staff nurses Debra Moset, 40, and Jessie Paya Jok, 44.

items.title: Haze bites: 14 areas nationwide hit unhealthy air levels, 11 of them in Sarawak alone
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 11 — A total of 14 areas nationwide, including 11 in Sarawak, recorded unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings due to haze as of 9 am today. Forty-nine areas nationwide were reported to have moderate air quality, while five areas recorded good readings. An API reading of zero to 50 indicates good air quality, 51 to 100 indicates moderate air quality, 101 to 200 indicates unhealthy air quality, 201 to 300 indicates very unhealthy air quality, while readings of 301 and above are considered hazardous.

items.title: Haze can’t stop the party: Sabah moves Malaysia Day celebration to SICC
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Sept 11 — The Sabah-level Malaysia Day celebration on Sept 16 would be moved to the Sabah International Convention Centre (SICC) due to haze. State Tourism, Culture and Environment Minister Datuk Jafry Ariffin said the change of venue was made to ensure the celebration could proceed as planned. Meanwhile, Jafry said Malaysia Day celebrations are being held by several agencies, particularly the State Archives.

items.title: Rosmah Mansor draws applause at Umno assembly as Najib’s clemency bid looms
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 11 — Datin Seri Rosmah Mansor, the wife of former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak, attended Umno’s general assembly today amid his bid for clemency. Umno president Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi then invited Rosmah to stand as delegates in Dewan Merdeka applauded and showed their appreciation. Rosmah was seated next to Zahid’s wife, Datin Seri Hamidah Khamis.
